reports.title: AKAMAI REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS

lines: Given our CIS momentum, track record of execution and continued strong pipeline, we expect Akamai's overall revenue growth to accelerate to 17% to 22% year-over-year when adjusted for foreign exchange* in 2027.
We expect further acceleration in 2028 with total revenue projected to exceed $7.0 billion,” Leighton added.

desk.headline: Revenue up 6% to $1.12bn, in line; adjusted EPS $1.77 beat but full-year outlook trimmed and Q4 revenue guide below estimates

other.label: Delivery and other cloud apps revenue
Capital expenditure
other.change: 41% of revenue vs 21% a year ago

results: Revenue grew 6% (7% in constant currency) to $1.12bn; cloud infrastructure services jumped 34% to $109m and security rose 9% to $622m.
The older delivery business shrank 3% to $391m.
Profit fell as costs rose: adjusted EPS dropped 5% to $1.77 and GAAP EPS fell 21% to $0.77; adjusted operating margin slipped to 25% from 31%.
Capital spending more than doubled to $464m as Akamai builds out cloud capacity; operating cash flow was $433m.
No shares were bought back in the quarter; cash and investments stood at $4.24bn. Over $14bn of multi-year cloud commitments were signed this year.

guidance.summary: Akamai narrowed its 2026 ranges with lower midpoints: revenue now $4.44–4.47bn and adjusted EPS $6.47–6.68. It also gave first targets for 2027 (17–22% constant-currency revenue growth) and 2028 (revenue above $7.0bn).

points: Management said large multi-year AI cloud contracts are ramping, with two of the first three big deals already producing revenue.
CEO Tom Leighton said delayed cloud revenue is not lost: it "just pushes to next year".
The CFO said space and power for the major deals has been secured, and expects margins to bottom in the first half of 2027.
About 25–30% of next year's cloud infrastructure revenue is expected in the first half and 70–75% in the second half.
Security products kept growing strongly while the legacy delivery business is being run for profit rather than volume.

watch: Timing of revenue from the large cloud contracts and whether more slips into 2027.
How low margins go in the first half of 2027 as capital spending stays high.
Whether security growth can offset the shrinking delivery business.
